name: Package for Thurman
summary: In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider needs her son Thurman’s tailoring supplies at Larson Clothiers in the Mage Quarter. He left home without his shears and needles, and Rema asks you to carry them to his workshop.

sections.title: A Mother's Errand
sections.body: Rema Schneider worries that Thurman will fall behind in his tailoring work without his shears and needles. He left home in a rush, and his mother asks you to carry the tools across Stormwind’s canals to his workshop.

sections.title: A Reluctant Apprentice
sections.body: Larson Clothiers is in the Mage Quarter, near the Mage Tower. When Thurman receives his tools, he admits he left them behind on purpose so he could skip his daily chores and have fun. Rema’s intervention ends his free afternoon, and he returns to his stitching.

faq.q: Who starts the quest Package for Thurman?
faq.answer: Rema Schneider asks you to carry a sewing kit to her son, who works in the Mage Quarter.

faq.q: Where can Thurman Schneider be found?
faq.answer: Thurman Schneider works inside Larson Clothiers in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter, near the path to the Mage Tower.

faq.q: Did Thurman actually forget his tools by accident?
faq.answer: Rema believes Thurman hurried out without his kit and asks you to bring it to him.

faq.q: What shop does Thurman apprentice for?
faq.answer: Thurman apprentices as a tailor at Larson Clothiers, a garment shop in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter run by the Larson family.

faq.q: Why does Rema Schneider ask an adventurer for help?
faq.answer: Rema believes Thurman’s apprenticeship is in jeopardy without his kit. Unable to leave her own obligations, she asks travelers heading toward the Mage Quarter to help.

faq.q: What happens after you deliver the sewing kit?
faq.answer: Thurman takes his kit and returns to helping the Larsons with their sewing.

angles.text: Every grand tailor starts at the bottom, running seams and holding pins. At Larson Clothiers, even an apprentice may wish to slip away from chores.
Stormwind’s ordinary citizens and artisans keep the capital clothed, fed, and running, one errand at a time.
